newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds swim up on global bond, Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds swim up on global bond, Greenspan.

text.p: Argentine bonds firmed late Tuesday as the market reacted positively to generally reassuring comments by U.S. Federal Reserve chief Alan Greenspan and to the spread for Argentina's global bond.
"Basically we are seeing a reaction to what Greenspan said and the improvement in U.S. bond prices," one trader at a foreign bank said.

He added the $2 billion global bond priced at a spread of 462.5 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries was also giving local bonds a boost. "They are arbitraging pars against global bonds to see if they can narrow the yield gap.
The Bocon Proveedor 1 due 2007 rose $0.625 to 99.75.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 1/2 to 89-7/8, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.45 to 125.625.
Greenspan's testimony to the U.S. Senate Budget Committee initially triggered a dip in U.S. Treasuries, but the market turned positive after it had digested what he said.
Traders early in the day hailed the Argentine government's success in placing the 20-year global bond.
In the money markets, call money rates rose to 5.60 percent from 5.55 percent.
